sonnet.problem: Card 3 just asked and answered that Joab questions David about letting Abner go. This card repeats the same fact ("What have you done?" and "questions the KING") for the same verse, so it adds nothing new.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Card 2 just asked and answered that David orders them to tear their clothes and mourn. This card repeats that order word for word, so it is a recap of the answer.
The card tells the mourning order for a murdered man, which is a heavy moment, yet it ends with a joke about Joab's sackcloth feeling heavy. That joke laughs at Joab and not with his human situation.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The question gives "hands not bound, feet not fettered" and asks how David says Abner fell. The baker can't reason this out. They can only guess the wording of the next line of the lament.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The statement makes two claims: the people take note, and they are unhappy. It should test one claim.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.
